..(Friday through Wednesday)
Issued at 410 PM EDT WED OCT 28 2026

The extended period opens Friday featuring unseasonably warm 
conditions initially, followed by increasing low-level moisture 
discrepancies as a weakening cold front sags toward the Ohio 
Valley. Aloft, broad southwesterly flow will dominate as 500 mb 
heights build to around 584 dam - placing values near the 90th to 
95th climatological percentile across eastern Kentucky. This 
anomalous ridge will support strong warm-air advection, pushing 
daytime temperatures into the lower 70s on Friday.

At the surface, this decaying boundary is expected to sag across
portions of the forecast area Friday before stalling and lifting
back north as a warm front Friday night into Saturday. Model
guidance diverges significantly regarding boundary-layer moisture
ahead of this boundary. Deterministic ECMWF runs aggressively
recover surface dew points from the low-to-mid 40s into the mid 50s
on Friday. However, other guidance favors a prevailing easterly 
to northeasterly component around the surface ridge centered to 
our northeast. This trajectory will maintain a feed of drier 
continental air near the surface. Given these boundary-layer 
winds, dew points were blended down a few degrees below the 
baseline NBM to limit an overly aggressive, premature moistening 
trend.

To our southwest, the remnants of Tropical Storm Vance - currently
in the Eastern Pacific - will weaken and lift northeast over the
higher terrain of Mexico Friday into Saturday, getting ingested into
the subtropical jet. Meanwhile, broader troughing over the western
CONUS will feature an upper-level low digging from the Pacific
Northwest into the Desert Southwest through the weekend. As this
western system amplifies and cuts off, it will tap that tropical
moisture plume and channel it northeastward Sunday into Monday ahead
of a deepening Central Plains cyclone.

For eastern Kentucky, this will translate to high and mid-level
clouds filtering in from the southwest late Friday afternoon and
evening, gradually lowering and thickening through Saturday. Despite
increasing clouds, unseasonable warmth will hold on across the
region for Halloween, with afternoon highs reaching the low-to-mid
70s - roughly 5 to 10 degrees above late October normals. Evening
conditions for prime trick-or-treat hours look favorable, featuring
rain-free, cloudy skies as temperatures fall from the upper 60s
around sunset into the upper 50s by midnight. Shower chances will
then ramp up from the southwest after midnight as temperatures 
settle into the lower 50s, with rain continuing to expand across 
the area through the day, Sunday.

Considerable uncertainty remains for daytime highs, to close out
the weekend highlighted by a 10 to 12+ degree ensemble spread 
across the area. The NBM has trended warmer, populating highs in 
the upper 60s to around 70, supported by the 12Z ECMWF in the 
lower 70s. Conversely, the 12Z GFS remains a cool outlier in the 
upper 50s, aligning closely with the NAEFS 10th percentile. This 
discrepancy hinges on boundary progression and rainfall onset. A 
quicker arrival of showers would lead to those unseasonably cool 
conditions, while a slower arrival would allow temperatures to 
warm into the 60s to near 70. Given the consensus between the NBM 
and ECMWF, leaned toward the warmer baseline, but this does entail 
a distinct bust potential.

Showers will persist through Sunday night before gradually tapering
off into Monday, with surface high pressure east of the forecast
area maintaining southeasterly winds and temperatures warming into
the upper 60s to around 70 degrees.

The Rex block pattern will hold firm across the Ohio Valley through
much of Tuesday, keeping eastern Kentucky unseasonably warm under
strong mid-level ridging. While the baseline NBM continues to
populate low-end slight chance PoPs (15 to 20 percent) on Tuesday,
this appears to be an artifact of timing discrepancies among
ensemble guidance, with a few faster members ejecting the cutoff low
seemingly premature. Given the strong subsidence beneath the 
anomalous ridge (NAEFS 500mb heights near the 90th percentile), 
expect Tuesday to remain largely dry, with afternoon temperatures 
climbing into the lower 70s.

Rain chances ramp up significantly Tuesday night into Wednesday as
the block breaks down and the cutoff low lifts into the Upper
Midwest and Ohio Valley, driving a strong cold front toward our 
region.
